subject.title: Bug: 180s compaction timeout is a single wall clock over the whole chunk pipeline with no partial-progress reuse, so a legitimately-long compaction fails identically every turn

question: Should OpenClaw accept a native compaction result produced immediately after its own safety-timeout cancellation, but only while the wrapper retains the exact timeout reason?
rationale: The implementation can mechanically distinguish timeout cancellation from user aborts, but accepting post-timeout session-state writes changes the product's failure and recovery contract.

options.title: Accept bounded timeout recovery
options.body: Allow the candidate PR's narrowly scoped timeout-owned commit window so usable progress can recover a wedged session.

options.title: Keep timeout results fail-closed
options.body: Retain inner chunk-progress preservation and clearer error guidance, but never commit a result produced after the outer timeout fires.

options.title: Require live gateway proof first
options.body: Hold the policy decision until a realistic slow-provider or full gateway compaction run demonstrates safe recovery.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded timeout recovery
recommendation.body: Allow the candidate PR's narrowly scoped timeout-owned commit window so usable progress can recover a wedged session.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked candidate PR is assigned to this person and prior review routes this exact policy choice there.
